chapter_title: Concerning the Four Things over which People kill each other.
chapter_note: The chapter is mostly a simple fourfold list plus concluding exhortation. ¶1 is a clear hagiographic/dialogue frame. ¶7 introduces a first-person admonitory voice with a ‘physician’ who separates Light and Darkness—this looks like later Manichaean homiletic expansion rather than the impersonal, systematic cosmological core. The oldest recoverable layer here is the fourfold list (food/sex/wealth/war) and its brief mortality conclusion.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue opening (“Once again he speaks to his disciples”) is Kephalaia frame apparatus.

paragraphs.core_text: The first thing is [the obsession] of people; in that they would eat [for the swelling] of their body [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal enumerative teaching (“The first…”) with no citation or institutional directives; part of a fourfold schematic list.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is [sexual inter]course; [...] fornication [...] fornication [...] men and women [...] in it with each other.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the enumerated fourfold; lacks frame/citation/institutional markers. Ethicized topic but presented as a structural ‘second’ item.

paragraphs.core_text: The third thing is wealth; and [...] the useless riches in [which] they shall pride themselves without [...] from it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumerative list item (“The third…”), gnomic/impersonal tone.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth is war; and the disputes, the [...] and the trials that they instigate against each other. Someone is victor over another, with each other in tyranny, so that they have received a name in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the fourfold scheme; still descriptive rather than prescriptive, with ‘name/glory in the world’ as a motive.

paragraphs.core_text: All people, they who side with these four major things that [a]re on every tongue [in the] world [...] they struggle so that they might generate them [...] among them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative generalization tied directly to the fourfold list; still impersonal and not church-institutional.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] he separates the Light from the Darkness, the good from the wicked;
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the homiletic first-person exhortation and self-referential/missionizing material (“However, I say to yo[u ... whoever wi]ll accept faith and invite it in together with this ph[ysi]cian whom I have brought…”, plus the concluding superiority claim over those who pursue the four worldly things). Kept only the cosmological separation clause as the oldest plausible teaching fragment.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Register shifts to first-person admonition and a ‘physician whom I have brought’ (rhetorical self-presentation typical of later homily/frame). Embedded within it is a compact, impersonal cosmological mechanic (separating Light/Darkness) that plausibly derives from older teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: For they will not remain with them for ete[rni]ty; rather they shall leave them behind and die.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Gnomic mortality conclusion to the fourfold-worldly items; no frame, citations, or institutional rules.
